name: Jozabad
overview: Jozabad was a male Levite who played a significant role among the leaders of the tribe of Levi. He is noted for his participation in the counting of the silver, gold, and utensils, demonstrating his involvement in the sacred duties and administrative responsibilities of the Levites. His leadership is affirmed in the records of Nehemiah, highlighting his standing within the Levitical community.
namesAndTitles: The name Jozabad means 'YHWH bestowed,' reflecting the divine blessing implied in his identity. This proper name does not appear to have been given directly by God but carries a meaningful connection to the Lord's provision and favor.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records that Jozabad was the son of Jeshua, establishing his familial lineage within the Levitical heritage. Beyond this, there are no additional family relationships documented, focusing attention on his tribal and leadership role.
scriptureSignificance: Jozabad's significance lies in his role as a Levite leader entrusted with the sacred task of accounting for valuable offerings, including silver, gold, and utensils. This responsibility underscores the trust placed in him to oversee the resources dedicated to the worship and service of God. His mention in both Ezra and Nehemiah situates him within the restoration period, contributing to the reestablishment of proper worship and temple service.
